lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Your target role is unclear.
items.because: The resume currently combines diesel mechanics, logistics operations, product management, an MBA, and student ventures.

items.says: The chronology raises questions.
items.because: The MBA overlaps with your Harbor Payments internship and with the 'Present' project; the internship also appears after a later full-time role unless the experience is intentionally reverse-chronological by relevance.

items.says: Several bullets describe activity rather than outcome.
Some metrics need clearer definitions or supporting context.
Your strongest product evidence is diluted by operational and mechanical experience.
Make the LinkedIn URL a clickable, professional link rather than displaying a generic or incomplete format.
Include a portfolio link only if it contains relevant product, analytics, or case-study work.
Do not include a full street address; city and country are sufficient if you include location at all.
Clarify whether the MBA is completed.
items.because: Since the date ends in June 2025, it should no longer appear as ongoing if you are applying after that date.

items.says: Consider adding a concentration only if it directly supports your target role.
If you had a particularly relevant leadership role, competition, or academic distinction, add it only if it strengthens your candidacy.
Because the MBA overlaps with the Harbor Payments internship and the Campus Food Rescue project, make sure those dates are accurate and clearly compatible with your full-time employment history.
If you are applying for product, operations, or business roles, explain why this role is relevant through the bullets or consider placing it in a separate 'Additional Experience' section.
The date appears immediately after an MBA ending in June 2025, which is plausible, but it creates a major question about your career direction.
If this is your current role and you are seeking to return to business or product work, your summary or cover letter should explain the transition.
If you are applying for mechanical or industrial operations roles, this experience should receive more prominence and technical detail.
Clarify whether 'under 5 days' is an average, target, maximum, or improvement from a previous baseline.
items.because: Without that context, the achievement is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: Consider adding the volume of jobs completed if substantial; fleet size alone does not show your individual throughput.
Verify that 'dry-dock time' is a standard term understood by your target audience.
items.because: If applying outside marine operations, the resume may need enough context for the accomplishment to be understood.

items.says: This is primarily a responsibility statement and is weaker than the first bullet.
Add measurable scale, such as number of systems, vessels, inspections, records, or compliance outcomes.
State whether the inspections were passed without findings, completed on time, or supported a particular regulatory requirement.
If you cannot quantify the outcome, consider shortening or removing it in a product/business-focused version.
'Owned' is vague unless you explain what ownership involved.
'The monthly review meeting that discussed them' describes meeting logistics rather than business impact.
Add the number of carriers, regions, managers, or shipments covered.
Explain what decisions resulted from the scorecards or whether performance improved.
If the meetings were merely administrative, remove this bullet or combine the work with a more consequential accomplishment.
Clarify the measurement period and baseline if possible.
items.because: A percentage reduction is more credible when the reader knows whether it occurred over one month or one year.

items.says: 'Pick errors' may be clear to logistics employers but less so to general business readers; retain it for operations roles, but consider adding context in a targeted version.
Define S&OP on first use if the resume will be read by generalist recruiters.
Clarify the forecast-error metric if possible, such as the type of error measure or what was being forecast.
'For 12 consecutive quarters' proves sustained ownership, but the result is more important; keep the duration only if space permits.
This bullet contains several separate accomplishments and may be too dense.
Clarify how the 1,800 hours were calculated and whether the savings were validated.

The relationship between the telematics contract and the driver-hour savings is not fully clear; make the causal link easier to understand through more precise description, without adding unnecessary detail.
Move this role according to chronology unless you have a deliberate 'Relevant Experience' structure.
items.because: A recruiter may otherwise wonder whether the dates are inconsistent.

items.says: Keep the internship near the top for product applications, because its relevance is higher than the mechanic role and possibly higher than the logistics role.
Your bullets currently include overlapping evidence about the checkout experiment and roadmap prioritization. Reduce repetition.
Be careful not to overstate your ownership as an intern. Use titles and responsibility levels accurately, especially for company-wide launches and roadmap decisions.
Clarify whether you personally designed the solution, partnered with design and engineering, or contributed to the redesign.
'Single verification step' may raise questions about compliance or risk controls; if relevant, indicate that the change remained within required controls.
Make sure the 2,300 merchants were all part of the measured pilot and that the before-and-after comparison is valid.
Clarify whether the 5-point increase is percentage points rather than percent; this distinction matters.
The phrase 'all merchants' is a very broad rollout claim. Confirm that it means all merchants in the relevant product, market, or company scope.
The later A/B-testing bullet repeats this accomplishment. Consolidate the technical experiment details into one place.
Explain what decision or outcome resulted from the prioritization.
Be precise about whether support tickets were a valid proxy for affected users or whether this was a deliberately chosen internal measure.
If the bullet has no resulting roadmap decision, launch, or business impact, it is less valuable than your outcome-based bullets.
This may be combined with the next bullet if both describe the same roadmap process.
The result is still somewhat vague: 'set the next quarter’s roadmap priority' does not tell the reader what changed or what happened afterward.
Clarify whether leadership approved the recommendation, whether a feature was built, or whether a measurable risk or cost reduction followed.
The sequence contains many activities; ensure the reader can identify the decision and its significance.
There is some overlap with the RICE bullet, so consider keeping the more outcome-oriented of the two.
This bullet is technically concerning.
Randomization by session may allow the same user to encounter both experiences, depending on the product and implementation. Explain or verify why session-level randomization was appropriate.
Reporting the effect 'on merchants’ customers' is potentially imprecise. The unit of analysis, experiment population, and affected party need to be distinguished carefully.
This appears to repeat the second bullet without adding a business outcome.
Unless you are applying for an experimentation, analytics, or growth role and can provide rigorous statistical detail, remove this as a standalone bullet or replace it with a distinct result.
If you retain it, include statistical significance or confidence information only if you can accurately support it.
Clarify whether 'funded' means approved budget, approved engineering capacity, or formally authorized rollout.
The 'Present' date should be updated if the project has ended or if the app is no longer active.
Clarify whether this was a real operating product, a student venture, or a classroom project.
items.because: The distinction affects how recruiters evaluate the results.

items.says: If the project continues, indicate your current level of involvement.
Clarify whether 3,100 students means registered users, eligible students, notified students, or total reach.
'With two dining halls' is ambiguous: clarify whether the app served two halls or whether two halls supplied the food.
Verify the 9-tonne measurement and explain whether it was weighed directly or estimated.
'First year' should have a clearly defined start and end period.
The arithmetic is correct: the increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: Correct the percentage or revise the underlying figures; this is an important credibility issue.

items.says: Clarify the measurement periods used for the before-and-after comparison.
'Chosen after 60 user interviews' implies the interviews directly established the feature decision. Make sure that causal claim is accurate.
The metric is ambiguous: moving from 75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point increase and approximately a 26.7% relative increase. Use the correct type of change consistently throughout the resume.
Clarify whether the volunteer shift system was your product intervention, an operational process, or both.
Add the measurement period if possible.
The project dates overlap with the MBA, which is expected, but make the academic context clear.
'Team Lead' is useful, but the resume should distinguish your personal contribution from the team’s overall work.
Clarify whether the $2.4 million was a modeled opportunity, forecast, or validated savings estimate. 'Sized' correctly suggests an estimate, but the distinction should remain clear.
If you know the implementation timeline, adoption status, or pilot budget, that could make the client outcome more concrete.
This is grammatically passive and primarily describes work performed rather than impact.
Quantify the reduction in form length, intake time, completion errors, or staff burden.
Clarify whether all four clinics adopted the changes and whether adoption was formally approved or simply observed.
If there was no measurable improvement, this bullet is weaker than the others and may be shortened or removed.
Make your individual role clearer if you led the mapping or redesign.
Avoid redundancy with the first bullet if both describe the same approval process; retain both only if one focuses on the financial case and the other on executive communication.
Clarify whether the pilot actually launched or was only approved. Do not imply implementation if you only received approval.
This section is currently too short and too generic for a product-management application.
Add only skills you can defend through the experience bullets.
Consider separating product discovery, experimentation, analytics, and delivery skills if you have enough relevant evidence.
'A/B testing' should be supported by accurate experiment-design knowledge, especially because the current resume raises questions about session-level randomization and measurement.
'Requirements writing' is useful but broad; clarify the type of artifacts you have actually produced if your target roles value them.

Your resume shows additional capabilities not listed here, including stakeholder management, process improvement, forecasting, vendor management, change management, and financial modeling. Add relevant categories based on the target role.
This is appropriate but underdeveloped.
Add proficiency-relevant tools only if you have genuinely used them in substantive work.
Consider including analytics, SQL, presentation, documentation, or experimentation tools if applicable.
Avoid listing tools without evidence elsewhere in the resume; recruiters may test them.
Excel may be less differentiating on its own unless paired with specific analytical capabilities or modeling experience.
